title: dedicated-gpu-pool-autoscale-debug-notes-breadcrumbs
content:
Context:
- Ongoing customer impact: intermittent request timeouts and elevated latencies for customers on Dedicated GPU pool 'dedicated-gpu-1' during business hours (approx 09:30-11:30 PST). Suspect autoscaler thrash + cold-warmup of GPUs.
- Observed behavior: throughput drops ~50% and tail latency spikes on short-running requests (~300-500ms normally -> spikes to 2s+). Backfills appear slow.

Timeline / quick breadcrumbs (notes to self):
- 2026-02-25 09:12 - First pager, partial outage.
- 2026-02-25 10:00 - Manual scale-up to 12->18 GPUs via rwdctl, immediate partial recovery.
- 2026-02-26 - 02:00 - autoscaler policy change rolled (cooldown reduced to 2m) (noticed in release notes).
- 2026-02-27 09:45 - Regressions returned.
- 2026-02-27 10:15 - Ran experiments (see commands).

Commands/traces tried (raw):
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated-gpu -l pool=dedicated-gpu-1 -o wide --show-labels
  -> Many pods in 'Running' but 'READY' 0/2 or 1/2 intermittently.

- kubectl describe node gpu-node-34
  -> "Taints: nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule" and lastScheduleTime shows frequent pod evictions.

- rwdctl pool describe dedicated-gpu-1 --json | jq '.autoscale'
  -> policy: {min:4, max:32, cooldownSeconds:120, scaleDownAgg: 1m} (note: cooldownSeconds set to 120 recently)

- curl -s 'http://prometheus.redwood.internal/api/v1/query' -d 'query=rate(rwd_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])'
  -> spike in requests per second followed by drop; node GPU utilization shows oscillation 10s->95%->10s.

- kubectl logs -n dedicated-gpu pod/dedicated-gpu-1-infer-abc123 -c runtime | tail -n 200
  -> repeated lines: "kv-cache-miss: warmup triggered for session X" and "alloc failed: OOM on cudaMalloc" around same timestamps as latency spikes.

- top / metrics: 
  - avg gpu_utilization: 76% when healthy, but during thrash windows shows sawtooth 8%->98% cycles every ~20-40s.
  - number of active worker processes per node drops from 4 -> 1 during spikes.

Error snippets copied: 
- "alloc failed: CUDA out of memory (caller=cuMemAlloc)"
- "pod eviction: node not ready, preemption in progress"
- "scale-down: removed 6 GPUs (cooldown active)"

Hypotheses / quick theories: (ordered by plausibility)
1) Autoscaler too aggressive on scale-down (cooldown too short). We recently reduced cooldownSeconds to 120s; warmup for model KV caches takes several minutes. Scale-down then immediate scale-up causes thrash and many cold sessions -> OOM/warmup stalls.
2) Warmup path is synchronous and blocks worker threads; if many sessions re-warm at same time, kernel memory allocation contention leads to OOMs and process restarts.
3) Node-level pod eviction / preemption due to resource oversubscription (GPU memory fragmentation or driver-level issues) causing pods to restart and lose warm KV cache.
4) Scheduling bin-packing causes pods to become concentrated on small set of nodes after scale events leading to hotspotting.

Reproduction steps (manual):
1) Set pool autoscale max to current and lower min to force scale-down on idle.
2) Hammer with small synthetic requests (short prompts) at 300 rps for 90s, then drop to 5 rps for 60s to trigger scale-down.
3) Observe whether OOMs / warmup logs appear on scale-up.

Investigations to run (next):
- Revert cooldownSeconds to 600s (10m) on a test pool and run the reproduction traffic pattern.
- Add staggered warmup to runtime (experiment branch) to avoid simultaneous KV cache fills: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842 (instrumented change).
- Add allocation tracing to CUDA allocator (verbose logs for fragmentation/OOM).
- Query Prometheus for per-node pod churn: rate(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[5m]) by node during incident windows.
- Check kube-scheduler logs for "Priority" or preemption messages matching timestamps.

Quick mitigation applied (temp):
- Throttled autoscaler by setting cooldownSeconds=600 on dedicated-gpu-1 (manual). Observed reduced thrash in next 4 hours, tail latency improved.
- Raised pool min from 4 -> 8 to keep some warm capacity.

Open actions / TODOs: (short)
- [ ] Run controlled repro on staging pool with cooldown=600 and instrumentation (Aisha + Marco)
- [ ] Merge staggered warmup PR and canary deploy to one pool (Ben)
- [ ] Add Prometheus alert for sawtooth gpu_utilization cycles and pod_eviction_rate (Priya)
- [ ] Postmortem draft (link to INC ticket) - include hypothesis test results

Notes / random friction observations: 
- Customers running many short-lived sessions (chatty product) are most affected. Longer-running sessions maintain KV cache and don't regress as much.
- rwdctl reports pool metrics aggregated; need per-node historical to debug properly (request: add per-node heatmap export).
- There is some suspicion that CUDA driver version mismatch on a node (gpu-node-21) correlates to more OOMs. Need to correlate node kernel/driver versions.

Related artifacts / references:
- INC-2026-02-27 (incident ticket)
- RED-2987 (autoscaler config change PR)
- runtime PR with staggered warmup: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842
- Slack thread w/ initial page: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02ABC123/p1612345678000

If I get pulled away: leave this as the single source of truth for the initial debug trail. Add timestamps when you run queries (prometheus, kubectl) so we can correlate.

-- Aisha
